title: Heat kills far more than fire does — but it kills in a way that doesn't trigger the emergency response.
explanation: France confirmed 2,025 deaths from the June heatwave on July 3 — three weeks after the heat had passed. A preprint estimated 20,390 dead across Europe in those same seven days. The Bordeaux fire burning simultaneously mobilized 2,500 firefighters, 1,500 soldiers, and weeks of front-page coverage. Heat and fire share a cause — the same Omega block, the same drought, the same record temperatures. They don't share a response architecture. Emergency systems are designed for disasters with perimeters: you can see where the fire is, you can evacuate a zone, you can call in air support. Heat has no perimeter. It kills overnight, in bedrooms, in the elderly and the poor, and the count isn't final until an epidemiologist runs the numbers in August.

evidence.text: France confirmed 2,025 excess deaths from the June 2026 heatwave — announced July 3, three weeks after the peak heat. A statistical preprint estimated the European continental toll at 20,390 for just the seven peak days of June 22–28: France 5,210, Germany 4,543, Spain 3,163, Italy 2,709.

The fourth US heat dome of summer 2026 targets 200 million Americans with overnight lows above 75–80°F through at least mid-August across the Southeast, Great Plains, Mississippi Valley, and Northeast. Maricopa County, Arizona has confirmed 40 heat-related deaths in 2026 by early August — a figure that grows as medical examiners complete retrospective reviews. By August 4, roughly 10% of the continental US has recorded its hottest day of 2026. When overnight temperatures stay this high, the body's core temperature repair cycle fails during sleep — 'heat debt' accumulates. The count arrives weeks after the deaths.

France deployed 2,500 firefighters and 1,500 soldiers to fight the Bordeaux fire — which killed no one confirmed as of containment on August 1. As the Bordeaux crews stood down, 1,500 firefighters moved immediately to a new Provence fire. Greece deployed helicopter fleets to Athens suburb fires — two crews died in a mid-air collision August 2. The firefighting infrastructure is fully mobilized. The June heatwave that killed 2,025 French citizens mobilized nothing equivalent.

retired_reason: Acute pattern resolved; heatwave death toll evidence from July 3, 37 days old.
